newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MONACO PREPARE FOR GERMAN STEEL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO PREPARE FOR GERMAN STEEL.

text.p: Monaco are bracing themselves for a different Borussia Moenchengladbach as the Germans fight for survival in their UEFA Cup second round second leg on Tuesday.
Borussia are 4-2 down after a home leg in which Monaco, who have scored four times in each of their last three games, hit them with some brilliant counter-attacks and clinical finishing.
But the French first division side's coach Jean Tigana is taking nothing for granted, expecting Borussia to do their utmost to keep German interest in the competition four-strong.
"The Germans never admit defeat," Tigana said. "They underestimated us in the first leg. They're going to show a different face and we'll have to be fully concentrated.
"It's up to us to kill the match. We'll have to worry them from the start...go out as if we were 0-0 and not change our game."

The Germans have to attack but they are also in danger of opening gaps at the back to be exploited by Brazilian Anderson and Victor Ikpeba of Nigeria, who between them contributed eight of Monaco's 12 goals in the last two weeks.
Monaco defenders Philippe Leonard and Franck Dumas are both in the squad after missing the first leg through suspension.
Metz, France's other representatives, travel to Lisbon to face Sporting with a 2-0 lead from the first leg.

The Portuguese side's Belgian coach Robert Waseige said: "We're at a two-goal disadvantage, which is serious, but two consecutive victories in the Portuguese league have given us the strength to overcome this handicap."
Italy's AS Roma are in a totally different position from Monaco against another German side, Karlsruhe, who won their home leg 3-0.
Roma captain Amedeo Carboni and Swedish midfielder Jonas Thern are both out with injuries.

Karlsruhe, without the suspended Thorsten Fink and Thomas Hengen, will be looking to contain Roma and reduce Italian interest in the UEFA Cup to at most two clubs, their Roman arch-rivals Lazio and twice winners Internazionale.

Both Italian sides travel with 1-0 first-leg leads, Inter to Austria where they meet Casino Graz, Lazio to the Canary Islands to face Tenerife, who managed a goalless draw against Real Madrid in the Spanish first division on Saturday.
Lazio have problems in defence with left back Giuseppe Favalli suspended, South African Mark Fish injured and Argentine Jose Chamot able to play only with a protective bandage on his left arm.
Tenerife's experienced German coach Jupp Heynckes has tasted defeat only three times in 39 home matches in European competition in charge of various teams.
One of his former clubs, holders Bayern Munich, are no longer in the competition after first-round defeat by another Spanish side, Valencia.
Valencia entertain Slavia Prague 1-0 up with their Croatian striker Goran Vlaovic recovering from a knock in Saturday's 3-2 league defeat at Barcelona.

Spain's third representatives, Espanyol, are without injured French striker Nicolas Ouedec and suspended Croatian Goran Bogdanovic for the difficult task of overcoming a 3-0 deficit away to Feyenoord Rotterdam.
Former Barcelona defender Ronald Koeman misses the match through suspension, while the Dutch also have midfielder Jean-Paul van Gastel out with injury until the new year.

Germany's UEFA Cup quartet also includes Hamburg, who are in a strong position 3-0 up on Spartak Moscow for the away leg in Russia, and Schalke with a slim one-goal advantage over Trabzonspor ahead of the away leg in Turkey.
Trabzonspor will, however, be without suspended Turkish international defenders Abdullah Ercan and Ogun Temizkanoglu.
England's sole representatives Newcastle United must curb their penchant for all-out attack at home against Ferencvaros of Hungary, who hold a 3-2 lead.
England striker Les Ferdinand, who scored their first goal in Budapest, said: "It's very delicately balanced and we can't go out all guns blazing.
"We just need the one goal and if we can get it and hold them we'll go through."
